A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CNTs can be encapsulated in the self-healing liquid monomers without affecting the self-healing properties of these materials, and the resulting materials can be used for restoring electrical and mechanical properties of damaged composite structures.

The main takeaway from our work is that

CNTs, which are known to be excellent conductors, are able to restore the electrical conductivity of self-healing materials, thus making them suitable for applications that require the restoration of the electrical conductivity of damaged materials.

the incorporation of microcapsules containing carbon nanotubes into polymer composites allows for a significant recovery of the electro-mechanical  properties after damage, thus making these self-healing composited highly suitable for aerospace applications.
the combination of self-healing and CNT-based conductive networks can provide a novel route for the design and development of multifunctional materials with improved electrical properties.
